structural_context: Summit Hotel Properties (INN) is a select-service lodging REIT (97 hotels, 14,415 guestrooms at 12/31/24) operating predominantly under Marriott / Hilton / Hyatt / IHG brands, with 41 of 97 properties (42pct) held in a 51/49 GIC Joint Venture with GIC (Singapore sovereign wealth, since July 2019). 53 hotels are wholly-owned. Stock at 2025-05-15 cutoff: 4.67 USD. 10-K filed 2025-02-24 reports FY2024 net income of 38.9M (vs -28.1M FY23) and same-store RevPAR +1.7pct YoY. Capital structure carries 1.4B consolidated debt incl. 287.5M 1.50pct Convertible Notes maturing Feb 15, 2026 with 10.95/share conversion price (134pct above 4.67 spot, functionally pure cash maturity). Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-04-30) confirms: (a) March 2025 275M Delayed Draw Term Loan closed to refinance the converts; (b) 50M Share Repurchase Program authorized Apr 29, 2025; (c) Q1 same-store RevPAR +1.5pct but mgmt flagged reduction in government-related travel and inbound international travel and tariff-driven sentiment risk. Group-3 delisted_or_distressed; central issue: highly-leveraged select-service lodging REIT with deeply OTM convertible refi forcing cash payoff during a soft-demand period.

rfm_tuples.R: The Convertible Notes will mature on February 15, 2026. We expect to complete the refinancing of the Convertible Notes prior to their maturity date. The initial conversion price is 11.99 per share; the conversion rate of the Convertible Notes was adjusted to 91.36 shares of common stock per 1000 principal amount of Convertible Notes at December 31, 2024 (implied conversion price 10.95 per share).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm 287.5M outstanding plus Feb 2026 maturity in debt schedule. Mode B: derive moneyness vs cutoff spot 4.67 and verify Q1 2025 refinance progress in subsequent 10-Q.

M_value.q1_2025_refinance_action: March 2025 closed 275M Delayed Draw Term Loan, undrawn at 3/31/25, to fund convert payoff

rfm_tuples.interpretation: 10-K is calmly confident (we expect to complete the refinancing) but the economics are coercive: convertible is 57pct out of the money at cutoff so holders will demand cash. INN responded by sourcing the 275M Delayed Draw Term Loan in March 2025 - only 275M against 287.5M principal, leaving a 12.5M cash shortfall plus interest, and the new facility will carry materially higher coupon than the 1.50pct it replaces (weighted avg rate already 5.06pct at 3/31/25). MODE rather than SEV because management did proactively refinance, but the disclosure understates the rate-shock-on-renewal cost embedded in this transition.

rfm_tuples.R: In September 2024, we executed an amendment to the 2023 Senior Credit Facility. Under the amendment, we may elect at our sole discretion that the Unsecured Leverage Ratio may exceed 60pct but shall in no event exceed 65pct for such fiscal quarter and the next three succeeding fiscal quarters (the Unsecured Leverage Increase Period). Same amendment executed in parallel for 2024 Term Loan.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm covenant amendment language in 10-K Note 6 and 10-Q Note 5. Mode B: identify whether the covenant cushion was actively needed.

M_value.right_exercised_as_of_filing: We have not yet made the election under the amendment

rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B tell: companies do not pay legal fees to amend credit facilities for a 500bp covenant cushion they do not anticipate needing. The 10-K disclosure that we have not yet made the election is honesty-credit but the act of negotiating the amendment in Sept 2024 (just as the convert refi window opened) is the structural tell that internal leverage models showed a forward path through 60pct. MODE not SEV because the cushion is in place; would escalate to SEV if Q1/Q2 2025 disclose actual election.

rfm_tuples.R: Quarterly cash dividend of 0.08 per share on our common stock and per Common Unit of the Operating Partnership. Dividends per common share: 0.30 in 2024, 0.22 in 2023, 0.08 in 2022.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm dividend trajectory in income statement. Mode B: compare current run rate to pre-COVID baseline and assess sustainability given convert-refi rate-shock plus soft demand.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Dividend recovering from COVID-era trough toward 0.08/qtr. Q1 2025 10-Q confirms board kept 0.08 on Apr 24, 2025 (16 days before cutoff). Mode B concern: a 6.85pct yield on a stock funding (a) a 5pct+ cost convert refi, (b) 65-85M FY25 capex, (c) 15.9M annual preferred burden, (d) 50M new buyback authorization - is structurally over-distributing given fixed-charge coverage. The dividend was the load-bearing we are healthy signal, but simultaneous announcement of the buyback (C5) and the rate shock from refi (C1) make sustainability through a tariff-driven demand soft patch the central uncertainty.

rfm_tuples.R: As of December 31, 2024, Aimbridge Hospitality or its affiliates (Aimbridge) managed 50 of our 97 lodging properties. Thus, a substantial portion of our revenues is generated by lodging properties managed by Aimbridge. This significant concentration of operational risk in one management company makes us more vulnerable economically than if our management was more diversified.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm 50/97 in property table. Mode B: search for Aimbridge counterparty disclosures (private; not an SEC filer, structural blind spot).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest disclosure (filing labels it significant concentration) but Mode B reveals the structural blind spot: Aimbridge is a private PE-owned operator, so we cannot verify their financial condition through SEC filings. Hotel-management-company distress (labor wage inflation, technology investment burden, staff turnover) would surface in revenue performance several quarters before it would surface in a Summit 10-Q. The 52pct concentration is itself a quantitative red flag the filing explicitly calls out, putting this at MODE not RED.

rfm_tuples.R: On April 29, 2025, our Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of up to 50.0 million of our Common Stock (the 2025 Share Repurchase Program). Repurchases may be made from time to time at management discretion. Currently, 50.0 million remains available for repurchases under the 2025 Share Repurchase Program.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm authorization in subsequent events. Mode B: stack against simultaneous 287.5M convertible cash refi, Sept 2024 covenant amendment, preserved common dividend, and 5pct+ interest rate on new term loan vs 1.5pct on retired converts.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital-allocation tell. Authorizing a 50M buyback (about 10pct of market cap) the SAME WEEK as filing a 10-Q that discloses a forced cash refi of 287.5M in converts at materially higher coupon, while preserving the 0.30 annual dividend and 15.9M preferred burden, while announcing 65-85M FY25 capex - is textbook announcement-without-execution tell. Management WANTS to signal undervaluation (buyback) and dividend sustainability (held at 0.08) to defend the stock during convert-refi window, but executing the buyback would consume the marginal liquidity needed for the refi shortfall plus rate-shock. Deterministic prediction is that 0 of the 50M will be deployed before the convert refi closes, consistent with the no obligation to repurchase disclaimer. SEV because the announcement effect is being captured without the cash-discipline cost - classic pre-distress capital-allocation pattern.

rfm_tuples.R: We own a 51pct controlling interest in 41 lodging properties through a joint venture with USFI G-Peak Pte. Ltd. (GIC), a private limited company incorporated in the Republic of Singapore. The GIC Joint Venture was formed in July 2019 with GIC. The Company serves as general partner and asset manager of the GIC Joint Venture and intends to invest 51pct of the equity capitalization, with GIC investing the remaining 49pct. The GIC Joint Venture intends to finance assets with an anticipated 50pct overall leverage target. Note 6: In February 2023, the GIC Joint Venture entered into an amendment to the GIC Joint Venture Term Loan to amend certain definitions, revise the minimum borrowing base interest coverage ratio and make certain other changes.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm 41 properties plus 51/49 economics plus Singapore counterparty in 10-K Note 3. Mode B: GIC is a Singapore sovereign wealth fund vehicle (USFI G-Peak Pte. Ltd.), not an SEC filer; verify whether 50pct leverage target is being met at JV level.

M_value.feb_2023_gic_amendment_purpose: revise minimum borrowing base interest coverage ratio (indicates pressure on coverage ratio)

rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B is the load-bearing finding. 42pct of INN hotel count sits in a JV with a Singapore sovereign-wealth-controlled vehicle that does not file with the SEC. Critical detail buried in Note 6: in February 2023 the GIC JV Term Loan was amended to revise the minimum borrowing base interest coverage ratio thresholds - that is a covenant relaxation at the JV level. INN consolidates the GIC JV (because it controls), so the 396M JV debt is on INN balance sheet, but the 49pct loss-absorption capacity sits with GIC. If the JV needs equity injections (rate shock, lower hotel EBITDA), GIC willingness to keep funding their 49pct becomes the swing factor. There is no honest M-source for verifying GIC intent because they are a private sovereign vehicle. SEV because this is the largest hidden tail dependency in the equity story, and the only thing the filing tells us (Feb 2023 covenant amendment) points to JV stress that was already material 2 years pre-cutoff.

rfm_tuples.R: During the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company recorded a loss on impairment related to a lodging property totaling 6.7 million to reduce the carrying amount of the property to its estimated fair value. Loss on impairment and write-down of assets: 6.723M (2024), 16.661M (2023), 10.420M (2022).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm impairment numbers in income statement. Mode B: stack against the FY24 gain on disposal (28.9M) and gain on extinguishment (3.0M) which render reported 38.9M net income substantially asset-recycling-driven.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding: stripping the 28.9M gain on disposal plus 3.0M gain on debt extinguishment from the 38.9M FY24 net income leaves 7M of operating-driven net income, BEFORE the 15.9M preferred dividend burden - meaning the FY24 underlying earnings to common were structurally negative (~-9M). The filing presents net income to common of 25.1M and a flattering we returned to profitability headline, but the math reveals that 60-80pct of that earnings is non-recurring asset recycling. For a REIT entering a forced convert refi at higher coupon, the FFO/AFFO trajectory is the load-bearing income claim, and the impairment-vs-gain symmetry is the structural tell that the portfolio is being right-sized via dispositions to fund the dividend rather than reinvested for growth. MODE not SEV because the disclosure itself is complete; framework objects to narrative softness around effectively negative core earnings.

rfm_tuples.R: We funded 89.3 million of capital expenditures and 5.2 million of development expenditures on a consolidated basis (FY2024). We anticipate spending an estimated 65.0 million to 85.0 million in capital expenditures across our portfolio (excluding the pro rata portion related to our joint venture partners) during the year ended December 31, 2025.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm capex in cash flow statement. Mode B: derive capex-vs-FFO coverage and capex-per-key adequacy for upscale select-service brand standards.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B coverage finding: FY25 capex guidance (65-85M midpoint 75M) is approximately flat-to-down vs FY24 (75.6M pro-rata) at a time when Marriott/Hilton brand-standard cost inflation is running mid-single-digits AND the company faces the rate-shock from convert refi. Capex represents 65pct of FY24 FFO - 65 cents of every dollar of FFO is required just for maintenance/brand-standard work, leaving very thin cover for the 0.32/yr common dividend (42M/yr), 15.9M preferred dividend, and refi-rate-shock. Most concerning: holding capex flat-to-down when revenue is also flat-to-down and government/international travel is contracting is consistent with a quiet under-investment cycle. Brand standards for Hilton/Marriott/Hyatt are not negotiable; deferring renovations now means larger PIPs in 2-3 years.

rfm_tuples.R: Total Debt: 1.408B at 12/31/24 (consolidated incl. JVs). Pro rata debt outstanding: 1.078B. Interest expense FY24: 82.6M. Weighted-average interest rate, after giving effect to interest rate derivatives, for all borrowings was 5.06pct at March 31, 2025.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm debt totals plus interest rate via Note 6 and Q1 2025 10-Q. Mode B: derive incremental interest cost from convert refi (1.50pct to about 6.5pct on 287.5M) and impact on coverage.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B quantification: replacing 287.5M of 1.50pct converts with 287.5M of 6.5pct term debt adds 13.6M of annual interest, which is 11.8pct of FY24 FFO (115.2M) and 32pct of the 42M common dividend. This is the single largest forward-earnings hit embedded in the filing, calmly disclosed across two filings (10-K and Q1 10-Q) without ever being headlined as we are taking a 13M+ recurring earnings hit in 2026. SEV because the disclosure is complete but the implication-discipline fails. For an income-vehicle REIT, a 32pct absorption of dividend headroom for refi rate-shock is the load-bearing forward-return-suppressor and warrants explicit MD and A treatment.

rfm_tuples.R: Q1 2025 10-Q MD and A: During the three months ended March 31, 2025, we experienced modest same-store revenue growth resulting from stable group travel and business transient demand which offset a reduction in government-related travel as well as inbound international travel. Changes in U.S. financial policies, including recently announced tariffs, have created uncertainty and volatility in the financial markets, which has had a negative effect on consumer and corporate sentiment.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm Q1 RevPAR +1.5pct same-store. Mode B: derive whether stable demand offsetting government and international decline implies a forward demand soft-patch through 2025.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Classic claim evolution / Mode B drift between 10-K (Feb 24, 2025) and 10-Q (Apr 30, 2025). In 9 weeks, the demand narrative materially softened: 10-K barely mentioned tariffs (boilerplate only); 10-Q has them as a load-bearing risk that could result in a reduction in near-term lodging demand. Government-related travel decline is particularly acute for select-service hotels in DC-area / capital city markets (INN has multiple Hyatt/Courtyard properties in these markets). The stable business transient and group demand which mitigated framing implies that without those offsets, same-store RevPAR would have been negative. For a highly-leveraged lodging REIT in the middle of a convert refi and a capex-light cycle, a forward soft-patch in demand is the single most dangerous macro tell. SEV because the 10-K narrative was meaningfully optimistic relative to the 10-Q-confirmed reality, and the gap surfaced in only 9 weeks.

preferred_arrearage_risk.trigger_for_2_directors: 6 quarterly preferred dividends in arrears (whether or not consecutive)

insider_form4_pattern_at_filing.interpretation: Form 4 cadence dominated by grant/withholding activity; no large insider open-market buys clustered to the convert-refi window (would be the bullish Mode-B signal) and no large open-market sells flagged. Net signal: neutral / no insider conviction trade either direction.

capital_allocation_red_flag.signal: Simultaneous 50M buyback authorization plus held common dividend plus forced cash convert refi at about 500bp higher coupon
capital_allocation_red_flag.framework_heuristic: When refi rate shock plus capex requirements plus preferred burden all bite simultaneously and management responds by ADDING capital-return programs rather than building liquidity cushion, this is the defend the stock during the refi window pattern that historically precedes distress

summary: Summit Hotel Properties (INN) FY24 10-K plus Q1 2025 10-Q: 10 R/f/M tuples scored. Severity counts: PASS=0, MODE=6, SEV=4, RED=0, UNV=0 (with PASS-leaning supplementals on auditor, going-concern). Honesty-alpha verdict: the filings are TECHNICALLY HONEST on every number (Big 4 auditor, full disclosure of covenant amendments, JV concentration, Aimbridge concentration, convertible refi mechanics, capex guidance, dividend trajectory) but consistently SOFTEN the NARRATIVE around what those numbers imply forward. The aggregate Mode B picture is structurally fragile: (a) 287.5M convertible refi forced as cash at about 6.5pct vs 1.50pct = 13.6M/yr incremental interest absorbing 11.8pct of FFO and 32pct of the common dividend (C1, C9); (b) Sept 2024 covenant amendment giving 500bp leverage cushion mgmt has not yet elected to use (C2); (c) 50M buyback authorized 16 days pre-cutoff while liquidity needed for refi shortfall (C5) - textbook defend the stock during refi window pattern; (d) 42pct of property count in opaque GIC JV with Feb 2023 covenant relaxation already on record (C6); (e) 9-week claim drift from FY24 10-K (calm) to Q1 10-Q (tariff plus government/international travel decline acknowledged) (C10); (f) FY24 net income is 80pct asset-recycling gains not operating earnings (C7); (g) Aimbridge 52pct management concentration in private operator we cannot verify (C4). Verdict NEUTRAL-leaning-SHORT: moderately-disclosed but structurally fragile lodging REIT entering coercive refi window during demand soft-patch. Framework correctly flags this as fragility-not-fraud (no RED).
framework_notes: Mode A (claim verification): the filing is consistently truthful on numerical disclosures. No Mode-A REDs. Big 4 auditor (E and Y); no going-concern; preferred dividends current; convertible refi mechanics fully disclosed.

Mode B (implied-verification derivation): the central Mode-B finding is the stacking of multiple individually-disclosed structural fragilities into an aggregate forward-return drag. The framework contribution is the CONNECTIVE TISSUE - recognizing that the convert refi rate-shock (C1/C9) plus covenant amendment (C2) plus buyback announcement (C5) plus asset-recycling-driven net income (C7) plus capex-light cycle (C8) plus Q1 demand softening (C10) are all simultaneous and reinforce each other.

Capital-allocation heuristic (new): announcing a buyback within the same filing window as disclosing a forced cash refi at higher rates should be treated as a SEV-tier capital-allocation tell. The structural prediction is that the buyback will not be executed in size; the announcement effect is the deliverable.

REIT-specific refi-coupon-shock heuristic: when a REIT convertible notes are more than 50pct out of the money at the maturity-year cutoff date AND the company has secured a backup cash refi facility, the incremental annual interest should be modeled deterministically and compared to (a) FFO and (b) common dividend. >10pct of FFO or >25pct of common dividend = MODE; >20pct of FFO or >50pct of common dividend = SEV.

JV opacity heuristic: when a US REIT has a 40pct+ property-count concentration in a JV with a non-SEC-filer sovereign or private partner, and the JV-level credit agreement has been amended to relax coverage ratios, this should be treated as a structural SEV regardless of how transparently the relationship is disclosed at the parent level.

Lodging-specific demand-decel heuristic: government-related travel decline plus inbound international travel decline acknowledged in a Q1 10-Q is a leading indicator for full-year RevPAR underperformance, especially for select-service brands in capital-city / convention / gateway markets.
process_rules_discovered: M-source gap: convertible-bond moneyness-vs-cutoff-spot scanner that flags any issuer with more than 100M of converts maturing within 12 months of cutoff date AND spot price more than 25pct below conversion price. INN would have triggered.

M-source gap: deterministic refi-rate-shock estimator that takes (convert principal, convert coupon, replacement term-loan rate proxy from peer issuance) and computes incremental annual interest as pct of FFO and pct of common dividend. The 32pct-of-dividend figure for INN is the cleanest forward-earnings drag signal.

M-source gap: buyback-announced-during-refi-window detector - flag any issuer that announces a buyback authorization within 90 days of a maturing debt instrument more than 5pct of market cap. Almost always an announcement-without-execution signal.

M-source gap: JV partner counterparty-opacity scanner - flag any 10-K mention of foreign sovereign, Singapore, Cayman, Bermuda, or private limited as a JV partner with more than 25pct of property/asset count concentration. This is structurally Mode-B unverifiable.

Heuristic candidate: claim drift in less than 10 weeks between 10-K and 10-Q on macro demand language as a SEV-trigger for cyclical industries (lodging, retail REITs, consumer discretionary). Compare specific phrases (tariff, government travel, inbound international, consumer sentiment) between the two filings.
